evals.prompt: With typescript-patterns loaded, implement a small behaviour change in a TypeScript module in a target repo (e.g. add a typed parameter with validation).
evals.expected_output: A scoped, strictly-typed change that mirrors the repo's conventions, adds tests (the repo's runner) covering the behaviour plus a boundary and an error case, and leaves tsc --noEmit and eslint green using the repo's own scripts and package manager.
assertions: The change is strictly typed: no `any` introduced and no unsound `as`/non-null `!` cast
Type-checks under strict on inspection (no type errors) with no new @ts-ignore/@ts-expect-error
Tests are added covering the happy path plus a boundary and an error case
When the repo declares a package manager (a lockfile or packageManager field) and scripts, those are used (not assumed npm)
No existing test is weakened, skipped, or deleted; no new eslint-disable and consistent formatting

evals.prompt: With typescript-patterns loaded, add async code that fetches an external resource and parses user-supplied JSON.
evals.expected_output: Awaited async with no floating promise, JSON narrowed from unknown into a typed shape (not used as any), errors handled by type, and deterministic tests that stub the resource and fake timers; no secret logged.
assertions: Every promise is awaited (no floating promise) and rejections are handled
Parsed JSON is validated/narrowed into a typed shape rather than used as any
Tests are deterministic (resource stubbed, timers faked; no real network/clock)
No secret or credential is logged or interpolated into log output

component.purpose: The TypeScript stack conventions and toolchain the software-engineer/qa-engineer (and the code-review lint aspect) apply when the detected stack is TypeScript; a lean, loaded-on-demand knowledge pack exercised through the software-engineer's Tier-2.
